summary: Bath County, Va. lookout: a steel tower was nearing completion on Flag Rock in 1929, now listed as gone. A public hiking loop reaches the overlook.

facts.design: steel fire observation tower, 35 feet high per a 1929 newspaper report

access.note: Hiking loop listed by Visit Bath County; land ownership not stated in sources.

visit.trail_note: 3.2-mile loop from behind the Milk House Market in Warm Springs to Flag Rock Overlook

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source found gives when it came down or what, if anything, remains at the overlook.

events.note: Steel tower nearing completion in October 1929, per a Harrisonburg Daily News report
Replaced an old wooden tower that had become dangerous

notes_for_editor: Check before publishing: a YouTube video titled Warm Springs Mtn. Fire Tower Exploration (youtube.com/watch?v=6UfdvsoIrrk) came up in search with a snippet describing a century-old fire tower on Warm Springs Mountain. Only the title was readable, so this is unverified. If it shows the 1929 Flag Rock tower still standing, the gone status is wrong. The 1929 report spells the place Warn Springs (apparent typo); the story uses Warm Springs. A Bath County Facebook group post lists Flag Rock among old fire lookout towers of the 1930s, but the page was login-walled and not used. The cached FFLOS Virginia index does not list Flag Rock. The Visit Bath County page does not mention a tower. Research used two websearch.py queries and about five page reads.
